content:
Surfacing a question from #FLT > CI failure (blueprint ruby issue).

Basically what happened was that Kevin Buzzard merged a dependabot PR that broke FLT because it included a package that was not compatible with the version of ruby specified in docgen-action. For now it looks like reverting that PR will get FLT working again, but I imagine that this will happen again.

At first, I opened docgen-action#27 to bump the ruby version to 3.4, but now I think it might be better to require downstream projects to specify their ruby version with a file like .ruby-version.

Tangential: we should probably start publishing versioned releases of docgen-action (and other frequently used actions).

I haven't used let alone contributed to that action so my opinion probably carries even less weight than usual, but it seem strange that projects need to know ruby is even involved. Perhaps actions/jekyll-build-pages can abstract that it even is? (Not sure I 100% fully follow why the ruby version changed, did Jekyll change it's minimum supported version?)

Tangential: we should probably start publishing versioned releases of docgen-action (and other frequently used actions).

(I think regardless of its prevalence that tagging versions of GitHub Actions is somewhat of a moral hazard).

Today was also my first time looking at the ruby part of the action so I'm not sure I know why things are the way they are either. As far as I can tell, the reason why the ruby requirement in FLT changed was because dependabot saw a Gemfile here and opened a PR bumping their versions.

I agree the pinning actions to SHAs is best practice and I generally try to do that when community repos use actions from outside leanprover-community. My thought was that releases with versions attempting to follow the semver rules could be a way of communicating breaking / non-breaking changes. Also, GitHub now has immutable releases which should make the existence of version tags less dangerous.

but it seem strange that projects need to know ruby is even involved

Well, there is a Gemfile checked in, so the coupling is already there. But I tend to agree with this statement in the sense that the users here are basically just following the instructions given in the docgen-action set up documentation, so we should try to guard against this, or at the least provide an escape hatch.

My suggestion is to:

(0) Add an instruction to the docgen-action README that tells people to edit the Gemfile to pin a ruby version (this will make dependabot not update with incompatible versions), and add a .ruby-version file with that same version. Maybe provide a shell script that people can run?

(1) expose ruby-version as an optional parameter to the action and just plumb it straight into ruby-version, falling back to a default value (which can even be .ruby-version if we are trying to enforce this in future versions of the action). Note that this parameter supports just specifying ".ruby-version" and it will pick that file up, so this would support that scenario.

(2) (a bit of a stretch, but why not) provide a skip-ruby-setup boolean parameter to support the scenario where a user might want to do this with their own parameters before invoking this action

If we don't have a decision here yet, I'd argue we should definitely merge https://github.com/leanprover-community/docgen-action/pull/27 , since 3.1 and 3.2 are end-of-life and not getting security updates anymore
I'm going to merge docgen-action#27 for now and then think harder about bigger changes.
